subject.title: [Bug]: opencode-go/minimax-m3 thinking content leaks to channel via Anthropic Messages path

question: For the opencode-go MiniMax-M3 Anthropic Messages path, should OpenClaw enforce source-side reasoning suppression, or should it preserve requested thinking and reject/filter provider responses that mislabel reasoning as ordinary text?
rationale: This choice determines the user-visible security boundary and compatibility contract for a third-party provider route; the issue and closed proposals do not provide current live protocol evidence that safely selects one mitigation.

options.title: Verify and set a provider-owned safe default
options.body: Capture the current request and stream behavior, then apply the narrowest opencode-go policy that prevents disclosure while retaining documented explicit overrides where the upstream contract supports them.

options.title: Preserve requested thinking with guarded filtering
options.body: Keep provider thinking requests intact and add a narrowly evidenced stream transformation only if the provider’s response format makes reliable separation possible.

options.title: Pause for upstream contract clarification
options.body: Defer implementation if the provider cannot distinguish final text from reasoning and no safe suppression or failure behavior is agreed.

recommendation.title: Verify and set a provider-owned safe default
recommendation.body: Capture the current request and stream behavior, then apply the narrowest opencode-go policy that prevents disclosure while retaining documented explicit overrides where the upstream contract supports them.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged prior MiniMax stream mitigation is the strongest available historical signal for this class of request and streaming behavior.
